conj:bohr-radius-categorical:
Conjecture Categorical Bohr radius a_0^{\mathrm{cat}} = \hbar/(m_e c\,\alpha_{EM}) (transported from QED virial-balance; categorical derivation open). Proposition. The dressed atomic transfer matrix T^{\mathrm{dressed}} \in H_n(q) with eigenvalues (q^{2k+1}, -q^{-(2k+1)}) at electronic shell k admits a candidate categorical length scale

  a_{0}^{\mathrm{cat}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\hbar}{m_{e}\,c\,\alpha_{EM}}

at which a postulated kinetic Markov-trace contribution \Phi_{1}^{\mathrm{kin}} and a postulated EM-coupling Coulomb contribution \Phi_{1}^{\mathrm{Coul}} are equal:

  \Phi_{1}^{\mathrm{kin}}(a_{0}^{\mathrm{cat}})
  \;=\;
  \Phi_{1}^{\mathrm{Coul}}(a_{0}^{\mathrm{cat}}).

Evaluating this candidate uses \alpha_{EM} = 1/(q\,[9]_q\,[10]_q) as the operator-selection LP weight of the EM force-carrier (prop:em-coupling-projection). The dressed transfer matrix eigenvalues derive from the B_3 dressing of the bare pe crossing. Evaluating a_{0}^{\mathrm{cat}} at q_0 \approx 1.11 yields 5.29 \times 10^{-11} m.

This formulation identifies the structural layer of Bohr-virial physics. It establishes the relationship between the dressed transfer matrix eigenvalue structure and the archimedean energy scale. The absence of a per-generator additive decomposition into kinetic and Coulomb components constitutes a Hecke-algebraic gap. This obstructs immediate categorical closure.

A full categorical derivation requires defining \Phi_{1}^{\mathrm{kin}} and \Phi_{1}^{\mathrm{Coul}} as Hecke-algebraic objects. Five algebraic strategies exist:

  1. Symbolic crossing-type tracking. Compute V_i symbolically in q. Track the contributions of intra-atomic dressed versus inter-atomic bare crossings as distinct monomials.
  2. Spectral-gap matching. Define purely Hecke-algebraic spectral gaps \Delta_{\mathrm{kin}}(k) := \log|q^{2k+1}/q^{-(2k+1)}| = (4k+2)\log q and \Delta_{\mathrm{Coul}} := \log|q/q^{-1}| = 2\log q.
  3. Length-grading of the Hecke algebra. Introduce an axiomatic length grading on H_n(q). Assign length \ell_b to bare generators \sigma_{i,\mathrm{bare}} and \ell_d \cdot (2k+1) to dressed generators \sigma_{i,\mathrm{dressed},k}.
  4. Gröbner–Shirshov spectral sequence decomposition. Decompose the molecular Markov trace via the spectral sequence (prop:spectral-sequence-collapse) and curvature-rank stratification (conj:curvature-rank-gb-stratification). The kinetic contribution appears at curvature rank 0. The Coulomb contribution appears at rank 1+.
  5. Functorial uniqueness from q \to 1 smoothness. Demand the archimedean realization functor commutes smoothly with the q \to 1 limit. This recovers the standard Hartree formula E_h = m_e c^2 \alpha_{EM}^2.

The Gröbner–Shirshov spectral sequence and symbolic crossing-type tracking are the primary paths to resolving the multiplicative mixing of the transfer-matrix update.

It bypasses the standard additive kinetic/Coulomb split. This provides a categorical recovery of this quantum result.

prose:intro-archimedean-hartree-crystal:
Evaluating the Hartree and mass-tower series over \mathbb{R} requires analytic special functions that realize the pre-archimedean z-Habiro cocycles. Through the archimedean realization functor \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}, the combinatorial branching of the Type-B folded Kashiwara crystal maps onto real-analytic dilogarithmic periods.

This section establishes the Bloch-group decomposition of hyperbolic knot complements over Bring's surface, details the Type-B folded crystal combinatorics, and develops the Clausen function \mathrm{Cl}_2(\theta) and the real-analytic Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm D(z).
conj:bring-hyperbolic-knot-bloch-decompo:
Conjecture Bloch-group decomposition of 2/(3\pi) from S_5-equivariantly embeddable hyperbolic knots in Bring's surface. There exists a finite multi-set \{(K_1, n_1), \ldots, (K_m, n_m)\} of hyperbolic knots K_i \subset S^3. These knots embed in Bring's surface X_{\mathrm{Bring}} respecting a finite-index sub-symmetry of the S_5 automorphism group. The multiplicities n_i \in \mathbb{Z} satisfy

  \boxed{\;\;
  \sum_{i = 1}^{m} n_i \cdot D\bigl[Z_{K_i}\bigr]
  \;=\;
  \frac{2}{3\pi}
  \quad\text{in } \mathbb{R},
  \;\;}

where [Z_K] \in B(F_K) is the Bloch class of K in its trace field F_K and D is the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm. Equivalently, the aggregate class

  [Z]_{\mathrm{Bring}}
  \;:=\;
  \sum_i n_i\,[Z_{K_i}]
  \;\in\;
  B(F)\otimes \mathbb{Q},

for F = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{15}) the compositum \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_3, \zeta_5), has Bloch-Wigner image D([Z]_{\mathrm{Bring}}) = 2/(3\pi).
prop:type-b-folded-crystal-combinatorics:
Proposition Type-B folded crystal combinatorics: c(\lambda) + c(\lambda^T) = 0 summand-by-summand. For every partition \lambda realized as a list of cells with contents c(r, \mathrm{col}) := \mathrm{col} - r, the cell-level content cancellation

  c(r, \mathrm{col}) + c(\mathrm{col}, r) = 0

lifts to the partition-level identity

  \sum_{x \in \lambda} c(x) + \sum_{x \in \lambda^T} c(x) = 0,

where \lambda^T is the transpose partition. Self-dual partitions \lambda = \lambda^T have content sum zero.
sec:archimedean-hartree-crystal-mass-tow: The analytic coherence of the Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm D(z) and the Clausen function \mathrm{Cl}_2(\theta) rests on the five-term pentagon relation in the Bloch group B(\mathbb{C}) = \ker(\nu)/\text{5-term}. This section constructs the Bloch-group quotient, establishes the \mathrm{Cl}_2 pentagon and partial Faddeev dilogarithm identities, and summarises the upstream real-analytic lemmas connecting polylogarithmic periods to the mass tower.
prop:cl2-pentagon-and-faddeev-partial:

rem:alpha-em-categorical-trace-ratio-int:
Remark Interpretation: \alpha_{EM} as h^2 over force-carrier categorical traces, and its role in the Hartree-energy conjecture. Interpretation. The trace-ratio identity (\alpha_{EM} categorical trace-ratio) refactors \alpha_{EM} from the inverse Bring complex complexity into the ratio of h^{2} over the product of force-carrier categorical traces. This shifts the \alpha_{EM} formula from an operator-selection-LP-cost interpretation to the q-dimension layer.

The structural picture requires two components:

  • For each force carrier T_{m,p}, the top-channel decoration is \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{m,p}) = q^{w} - q^{-w} with w = (m-1)p, read off the trivial channel of the m-strand realisation.
  • The inverse product of these two traces, rescaled by h^{2}/q, yields \alpha_{EM}.

The h^{2} numerator originates from the two (q - q^{-1}) factors in the denominators of [9]_q and [10]_q.

Significance for the Hartree-energy conjecture. This identity supplies the algebraic mechanism introducing \alpha_{EM}^{2} into the binding energy. The molecular bound state projects onto the Wedderburn channels (3, 1) and (2, 1, 1) with non-trivial \delta_q weight (Force carrier T_{p,q} acting on n-strand braid lands on Wedderburn channel \lambda = (p, 1^{n-p})).

Squaring the trace-ratio identity yields:

  \alpha_{EM}^{2}
  \;=\;
  \frac{h^{4}}{q^{2} \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{2,9})^{2} \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{3,5})^{2}}.

The bound-state Markov trace contribution is bilinear in the characters \chi_{(3,1)} and \chi_{(2,1,1)}. Conjecturally, these characters are proportional to \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{3,5})^{-1} and \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{2,9})^{-1}. This bilinearity provides the categorical analogue of the Coulomb potential. Their product supplies the \alpha_{EM}^{2} factor.

Closing this algebraic identity constitutes the next step for Conjectured categorical derivation of E_h = m_e c_q^2 \alpha_{EM}^2.
prop:alpha-em-shift-multiplicative-chain:
Proposition Multiplicative-chain index identity: [\alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{2,9})]_q [\alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{3,5})]_q = [9]_q [10]_q.

The torus-knot shift exponents of the shift proposition take the values

  \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{2,9}) = 9, \qquad \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{3,5}) = 10 .

Hence the chain form agrees with the bare form of the EM coupling projection:

  q \cdot
  \bigl[\alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{2,9})\bigr]_q \cdot
  \bigl[\alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{3,5})\bigr]_q
  \;=\;
  q \cdot [9]_q \cdot [10]_q .

That this product is \alpha_{EM}^{-1} is the claim of the EM coupling projection, not of this proposition.
prf:alpha-em-shift-multiplicative-chain:
Proof Proof of alpha em shift multiplicative chain. The identity composes two named identities:

  1. Electromagnetic coupling from the antisymmetric braiding and force-carrier crossings establishes the bare combinatorial form:

      \alpha_{EM}^{-1} \;=\; q \cdot [9]_q \cdot [10]_q.

    This is derived from the antisymmetric eigenvalue -q^{-1} of the R-matrix and the q-deformed crossing numbers of the force-carrier generators T_{2,9} and T_{3,5}. By (T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}) is the unique pair of genus-4 torus knots, this basis consists exactly of the genus-4 saturating torus-knot set on \Sigma_4.

  2. Pole order at q=0 of the torus-knot character: \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{p,k}) = k(p-1) on V_{(1^p)} establishes the closed-form identity:

      \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{p,k}) \;=\; k(p-1)
  \qquad (\gcd(p, k) = 1)

    on the all-anti-symmetric channel V_{(1^p)}. Specialise at (p, k) \in \{(2, 9), (3, 5)\}:

      \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{2,9}) \;=\; 9 \cdot 1 \;=\; 9,
  \qquad
  \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{3,5}) \;=\; 5 \cdot 2 \;=\; 10.

Substituting these values into the bare formula yields the stated identity exactly:

  \alpha_{EM}^{-1}
  \;=\; q \cdot [9]_q \cdot [10]_q
  \;=\; q \cdot \bigl[\alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{2,9})\bigr]_q
              \cdot \bigl[\alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{3,5})\bigr]_q.
  \qquad \square

conj:schwinger-measure-computational-tim:
Conjecture Computational-time identification: the binding Borel variable is the loop proper time. Let s denote the Schwinger proper-time variable of the \zeta-regularized one-loop photon determinant on the Bring Jacobian, whose loop expansion weighs proper time by the scale-invariant measure \varsigma\,\frac{ds}{s} with unit \varsigma. Let N(n) denote the binding normalizer forced by the normalization bridge — the unique strip N(n) = (n-1)! making the binding generating function the carrier of the proved depth-2 confluent kernel (the normalization leg of The q-difference kernel R is the jet-prolongation symbol, carried by the binding q-lift module).

The framework premises are named:

  • P1 (scale-freedom): the substrate is scale-free; the locally realized modulus q_0 is local data, not a structural scale of the substrate.
  • P2 (computational time): proper time is computational time — s counts the substrate's computation steps.

Statement. The binding sector's Borel variable and the loop's Schwinger proper time s are the same substrate object. Under P2 both are the substrate's computational time, and the identification takes the quantitative form: the normalizer is the n-th moment of the loop's proper-time measure,

N(n) \;=\; \int_0^\infty s^{\,n}\, e^{-s}\,\varsigma\,\frac{ds}{s} \;=\; \varsigma\,(n-1)! .

Conditional consequences. Both are conditional on this conjecture (together with P1/P2 where noted); neither is a derivation of it.

  1. The unit is forced: \varsigma = 1. The proved identity n \cdot N(n) = n! rescales under a unit \varsigma to \varsigma \cdot n! = n!, so \varsigma = 1 exactly; the rival value \varsigma = \tfrac12 gives n!/2 \neq n! (an exact distinguisher, proved unconditionally). Conditionally, this fixes the unit — one nat per proper-time e-fold, with k_B = 1 so that entropy is counted in nats.
  2. The \tfrac12 is located per-channel bar-even. With total unit \varsigma = 1, the working per-channel coefficient \tfrac12\,a_0 = 1/(8\pi) — where a_0 = 1/(4\pi) is the derived two-dimensional heat-kernel unit entering the \alpha_{EM} insertion (\alpha_{EM} as the root of the self-consistent fixed-point cubic) — arises from the doubled-pair channel split. For the doubled bar pair (q, q^{-1}) \leftrightarrow (t, 1/t) and a bar-even integrand f, i.e. f(t) = f(1/t) under the bar involution t \mapsto 1/t, the exact fold identity \int_0^\infty f(t)\,\tfrac{dt}{t} = 2\int_1^\infty f(t)\,\tfrac{dt}{t} places the \tfrac12 per channel on the bar-even side, while a bar-odd integrand receives 0. This tips the \tfrac12-adjudication toward the \rho-split reading (total unit one, the \tfrac12 in the channel split) and against the energy-Jacobian reading (\varsigma = \tfrac12 on the proper-time side), which would break the moment identity.

The identification is a dictionary premise between two sectors — the \alpha_{EM} loop measure and the binding q-Borel transform. It is stated here as a precise, falsifiable structural claim: a derivation would fix the unit; a refutation would rule the identification out. The two sectors would share one unit, and the binding side's is forced by a proved identity; the checkable content is the moment identity above, verified exactly at orders n = 1 through 6.

Fibre-level refinement (bar-parity). The statement above is archimedean (q = 1), where the proper time s is real and hence bar-invariant. At the fibre level (q \neq 1) the identification is consistent only in the balanced q-Borel convention: the one-sided normalizer [n-1]_q! is bar-covariant with exact weight q^{-(n-1)(n-2)/2}, so it cannot equal a bar-invariant proper-time object, while the balanced normalizer q^{-(n-1)(n-2)/4}\,[n-1]_q! is exactly bar-invariant with vanishing first-order q-correction. The conjecture is therefore to be read in the balanced convention; the one-sided reading is refuted at q \neq 1 (exact weight mismatch, machine-verified at both substrate pins).

Structure of the open content. The binding generating function enters this paper only formally — the proved normalizer strip, the proved depth-2 recurrence, and formal q-Borel coefficient maps; no binding number is produced by an integral resummation. The conjecture's representability content is therefore a claim about a canonical choice of integral representation for a formally performed operation, and under that reformulation its two levels separate into distinct problems.

  • Archimedean (q = 1): closed. The proper-time kernel is derived, not chosen: e^{-s}\,ds is the unique positive measure whose \frac{ds}{s}-moments are (n-1)! (Carleman determinacy), and the explicitly constructed family of balanced fibre kernels converges weakly to it — tightness is proved from the second-moment confluence, so every Prokhorov subsequential limit is the Schwinger measure (conditional only on the classical Prokhorov-selection and moment-passage theorems, which are taken as hypotheses).
  • Fibre (q \neq 1): the choice has exact coordinates. The balanced moment functional determines a canonical Jacobi operator J(q) with no convention entering (Favard); the balanced moment problem is indeterminate at q \neq 1, J(q) has deficiency indices (1,1), and its self-adjoint extensions form a circle whose spectral measures are exactly the representing kernels. Three prior descriptions of the ambiguity are one object in three frames: the translate continuum u \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}/\tilde q^{\,\mathbb{Z}} of theta-grid kernels (\tilde q = \sqrt{q}), the nonzero Poisson dual-mode sector of a single log-normal Gaussian — the atomic kernels are its lattice samplings, the absolutely continuous kernel its zero mode — and the self-adjoint-extension circle itself.
  • The closing question, named. What remains open is the distinguished extension. The moment functional is Stieltjes, so the Friedrichs and Krein extensions are canonical candidates requiring no further input. The bar-involution route as first posed is closed in its pushforward reading: the reflection s \mapsto \tilde q^{-1}/s does not act on the extension circle by pushforward at all — the image of an extension measure has bounded support, so its moments grow too slowly to represent the balanced sequence — hence it cannot exchange the extremal extensions in that reading; an action on the Nevanlinna parameter not induced by pushforward remains open. Two structural inputs replace it. First, the family is identified in the classical literature: the balanced kernel family factors exactly as a Stieltjes–Wigert log-normal core — Stieltjes' 1894 indeterminate example at base \sqrt{q} — convolved with a determinate compact Jackson factor, and the one-sided convention is exactly Moak's q-Laguerre family under a pure scaling. Second, as measured: the Friedrichs and Krein atom supports occupy complementary \tilde q-sublattices whose common translate class extrapolates to the unit class u \equiv 1; the bar-fixed classes are proved to be exactly \{1, \tilde q^{1/2}\}, so the measured alignment lands on one of the two symmetric points. The sharpened open content: derive the extension choice (Friedrichs versus Krein) from substrate structure, or derive the u \equiv 1 alignment that is at present only measured.

The second route reduces to a single analytic statement. For the pure Stieltjes–Wigert core the extremal extensions are explicit: its Jacobi data have the closed form \alpha_k = \tilde q^{\,k-1}(\tilde q^{\,k}(1+\tilde q) - 1), \beta_{k+1} = \tilde q^{\,3k}(\tilde q^{\,k+1} - 1) — proved at general order (the iterated Jacobi vector in closed form, hence (M^n)_{00} = \tilde q^{\,n(n-1)/2} exactly) — and the Nevanlinna function is the Ramanujan entire function A_{\tilde q^{-1}} up to a constant, so the Krein extension is supported on its zeros and the Friedrichs extension on those zeros shifted by exactly one \tilde q-step; the two occupy complementary sublattices of the integer \tilde q-lattice class.

Transporting that class to the balanced family requires no perturbation argument. Comparing the two families through their moment ratios rather than their Jacobi data makes the transport exact: the factorization gives m_{k+1}/m_k = \tilde q^{\,k} E (1 - p^{\,k+1}) against the core's exact \tilde q^{\,k}, so the class shift is exactly \log_{\tilde q} E with E = q/(q-1), and the whole discrepancy is the single closed-form term \log_{\tilde q}(1 - p^{\,k+1}), which vanishes geometrically. Both ratio identities and the vanishing are proved. Hence the balanced tropical class is \varphi_1 = \log_{\tilde q} E \bmod 1 — the unit class — by derivation.

What remains is one analytic statement: that the extremal supports are asymptotic to those ratios. It is the same input the pure Stieltjes–Wigert core already requires (the asymptotics of the zeros of A_{\tilde q^{-1}}), so the transport introduces no further analytic debt. Numerically the conclusion holds to 8 \times 10^{-10} at q = 2.0736 and remains consistent, though not certified, on rungs approaching the substrate; at the pins the core certifies but the balanced truncation does not, so no class is claimed there.

  • Selection principles tested (exact outcomes). Singularity matching is uniquely selective in form — a single off-axis output pole datum would pin the kernel exactly — but is data-blind on the data available here: the fibre q-Borel transform is entire, and the only computable output singularity (the positive-axis wall) is exactly translate-invariant; the two reflection-symmetric candidates differ by exactly half a \tilde q-step in the model pole lattice, so a future output datum would discriminate them sharply. Modular-double covariance organizes the family — the family is the dual-frame decomposition of one Gaussian — but does not select: strict self-duality is empty at the substrate, reality of the dual modes re-derives the bar-reflection cut, and the two natural strengthenings (dual-mode positivity; modular inertness) each pin a unique kernel, but different ones.

Nothing downstream depends on this. The conjecture is unchanged in kind; its open fibre content is relocated, with exact coordinates, from the choice of kernel to the choice of self-adjoint extension.
def:schwinger-measure-unit:
Definition Schwinger proper-time measure and its unit \varsigma. The Schwinger proper-time measure with unit \varsigma is the scale-invariant density on the proper-time half-line,

\mu_\varsigma \;=\; \varsigma\,\frac{ds}{s}, \qquad s \in (0, \infty),

where s is the Schwinger proper-time variable of the one-loop determinant and the scalar \varsigma is the Schwinger measure unit. The shape is rigid: a density f satisfying the scale-invariance functional equation f(\lambda s)\,\lambda = f(s) equals f(1)/s, so \mu_\varsigma is the unique scale-invariant choice up to the single scalar \varsigma.

The canonical unit is \varsigma = 1: in the logarithmic coordinate the measure of one e-fold [s, e\,s] is exactly \varsigma, and with k_B = 1 (entropy in nats) the unit is denominated in nats per proper-time e-fold. Downstream consumers reference this result for the per-loop measure normalization; under the canonical unit and the per-channel \tfrac12 split, the working per-channel coefficient is \tfrac12 \cdot \frac{1}{4\pi} = \frac{1}{8\pi}.

Conjectural backing of canonicity. Defining \mu_1 names a construction; the canonicity of the choice \varsigma = 1 is not proved. It is conditionally forced by the computational-time identification Computational-time identification: the binding Borel variable is the loop proper time, through the moment identity n \cdot N(n) = n! for the binding normalizer N(n), and, separately, by the framework premises P1 (substrate scale-freedom) and P2 (proper time as computational time) stated there. Unconditionally it remains a unit convention of the same species the framework canonizes elsewhere for discrete time steps. Empirical support is exact rather than numerical: the unit-measure moment identity holds at orders 1 through 6, and a pin-invariance falsifier eliminates every intrinsic per-step rival unit.

Notation. The unit is written \varsigma (varsigma). The notation register reserves plain c for color, with c_q and c_k also taken, so this paper uses \varsigma.
rem:schrodinger-color-falsifiability:
Remark Schrödinger's color metric, diminishing returns, and a falsifiable q_0 prediction. The categorical q-chromaticity construction yields a falsifiable prediction regarding human color perception. This challenges the Riemannian paradigm [schrodinger1920color] and aligns with the modern psychophysical results of Bujack et al. [bujack2022].

The empirical result (Bujack et al., 2022).

Bujack et al. [bujack2022] report experimental evidence that perceived color differences violate Riemannian additivity along geodesics. The observed differences satisfy the strict inequality:

  \Delta E(A, B) + \Delta E(B, C) > \Delta E(A, C).

This diminishing-returns principle contradicts the assumptions of Riemann, Helmholtz, and Schrödinger [schrodinger1920color]. A crowdsourced color-triad experiment (75{,}896 training trials across ten splits, R^2 = 0.556, F(3, 60) = 25.00, p < 0.001) yielded a negative average-difference coefficient (\beta_{\bar d} = -0.005, t(60) = -5.566, p < 0.001) [bujack2022, Results, Table 1]. Among the parameterized scaling candidates in [bujack2022, Eq. (18)], the logarithmic model f_{\log}(\Delta\psi) = b\log(a\Delta\psi + 1)/\log(a + 1) matched the flexible monotonic spline in predictive accuracy, leading Bujack et al. to propose a second-order Weber–Fechner law in which perceived differences grow logarithmically at large stimulus separations [bujack2022, Discussion]. Prior psychophysical studies fit perceived color differences to a power law with an exponent near 0.5.

The categorical prediction.

The Skein relation q[L_+] - q^{-1}[L_-] = (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})[L_0] deforms the distance on the q-chromaticity simplex. The distance inherits a non-Riemannian correction matching the quantum-integer arc-length:

  \Delta E_{\mathrm{perc}}(d)
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{\eta}\,\mathrm{arsinh}\!\bigl(\eta\,d\bigr),
  \qquad
  \eta := \frac{q - q^{-1}}{2}.

Here d denotes the Riemannian chord length, and \Delta E_{\mathrm{perc}} denotes the perceived geodesic difference. This function constitutes the unique analytic one-parameter extension of [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}) to a projective chromaticity 2-simplex metric. The limit \eta \to 0 recovers the purely Riemannian metric \Delta E_{\mathrm{perc}} = d.

See Table 1.

The large-d logarithmic asymptote precisely matches the second-order Weber–Fechner law suggested by [bujack2022]. The empirical power-law exponent of \approx 0.5 captures the intermediate-d behavior of \mathrm{arsinh}(\eta d)/\eta, mapping the transition between the linear and logarithmic regimes.

Numerical prediction from the substrate parameter.

Evaluation at the proton-pinned substrate value q_0 = 1.1099785827513808\ldots determines \eta and the crossover scale d^{\,*}:

  \eta = \frac{q_0 - q_0^{-1}}{2} = 0.10453015\ldots \approx 0.1045,
  \qquad
  d^{\,*} := 1/\eta = 9.5666179\ldots \approx 9.57.

On this reading the transition from Riemannian to Weber–Fechner scaling occurs near \Delta E \approx 9.57 on a normalized L^{*}-style scale. The cited experiment does not measure a crossover scale, so it neither corroborates nor refutes this value. In its regression the two coefficients indexed by the difference of differences, \beta_{\Delta d = 5} = 0.048 (t(60) = 2.815, p = 0.010) and \beta_{\Delta d = 10} = 0.119 (t(60) = 6.632, p < 0.001), are level effects of \Delta d, not the onset of diminishing returns at a particular scale. The only diminishing-returns coefficient is \beta_{\bar d} = -0.005, and the authors read its negativity as weak support for nonadditivity, conditional on the L^{*} axis being nearly perceptually uniform, an assumption they note may not hold due to background crispening [bujack2022, Results, Table 1; Fig. 7]. The crossover scale d^{\,*} \approx 9.57 therefore has no empirical comparison in that source.

Falsifiability protocol.

The categorical prediction forms a one-parameter family \Delta E_{\mathrm{perc}}(d) = \mathrm{arsinh}(\eta d)/\eta. A high-precision color-perception experiment can fit \eta to a confidence interval [\eta_-, \eta_+]. This forces three possible outcomes:

See Table 2.

An inconsistent measurement falsifies the hypothesis that retinal \Delta E directly measures the Skein metric on the Bring-surface chromaticity simplex. It leaves the broader framework intact, because color perception operates several decoherence layers above the substrate.

Sign and functional-form predictions.

The framework makes three qualitative predictions already confirmed by [bujack2022], independent of numerical fitting:

See Table 3.

The final empirical test lies in measuring the magnitude of \eta.

Connection to confinement.

The deformation parameter q - q^{-1} = 2\eta determines the magnitude of the forced negative coefficients driving color confinement. Measuring \eta \approx 0.10 via macroscopic color perception provides an independent measurement of the substrate deformation governing quark confinement.

prose:intro-integer-stability-diophantin: On the discrete nuclear lattice \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^2 of proton and neutron counts (Z, N), minimizing the six-term categorical mass functional at fixed mass number A = Z + N defines an arithmetic curve—the Diophantine valley of stability. This section proves the integer-stability theorem, derives the Diophantine valley equation from the balance between the symmetric Wigner Jucys–Murphy energy and the topological Coulomb pairing, and establishes structural stability of the valley under small perturbations of the modulus q_0.
prop:integer-stability:
Proposition Integer stability: the valley of stability as a Diophantine constraint. Physical nuclei require integer proton and neutron numbers. Stable hadrons correspond to integer solutions of a quadratic energy minimisation. The continuous optimum p^*(A) defines the beta-stability line.

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be the Descartes universe with substrate parameter q. At a fixed mass number A = Z + N, the nuclear binding energy is a strictly convex quadratic in the proton number p:

  E(p, A) = 
  \underbrace{\left(\frac{a_C}{A^{1/3}} + \frac{4a_A}{A}\right)}_{\alpha(A)} p^2
  - \underbrace{4a_A}_{\gamma} p
  + \delta(A),

where a_C = \lambda_C is the Coulomb coefficient and a_A = a_{\mathrm{asym}} the Pauli asymmetry coefficient of beta stability, the p-dependent part is that of a_C\,p^2/A^{1/3} + a_A (A - 2p)^2/A, and \delta(A) collects terms independent of p.

The continuous minimum is

  p^*(A) =  \frac{\gamma}{2\alpha(A)} =  \frac{A}{2 + \dfrac{a_C}{2a_A} A^{2/3}}.

Because E is strictly convex in p, the exact integer minimiser p_{\mathrm{stab}}(A) is one of the two nearest integers to the continuous minimum:

  p_{\mathrm{stab}}(A) = \mathrm{argmin}_{p \in \{0, 1, \ldots, A\}} E(p, A) \in \bigl\{\lfloor p^*(A) \rfloor, \lceil p^*(A) \rceil\bigr\}.

Archimedean specialisation. The binding energy E(p), its continuous optimum p^*, and the convex-minimisation argument are stated over \mathbb{R}. The integer-minimiser bound relies on the real ordering.
rem:integer-stability-novelty: Remark Mathematical novelty of the integer-stability pairing rigidification. Algebraic rigidification. Nearest-integer minimization reframes even-even dominance algebraically. The empirical observation stems from a rigid convex optimization over the quantum integers. This argument supplements standard liquid-drop models.
rem:diophantine-valley:
Remark The valley of stability as a Diophantine approximation problem. The nuclear stability problem is a Diophantine problem on an algebraic curve. Stable hadrons are precisely the integer solutions to an equation derived from the Skein binding Lagrangian.

The stability cubic.

Substituting t = A^{1/3} into the beta-stability line p^*(A) = A/(2 + cA^{2/3}) of beta stability and clearing denominators yields the stability cubic:

  t^3 =  p(2 + ct^2),
  \qquad
  c = \frac{a_C}{2a_A}.

This plane curve \mathcal{S} \subset \mathbb{A}^2 parametrizes the locus of beta-stable nuclei in the (p, t)-plane. The physical nuclei are the integer points of \mathcal{S}: pairs (p, A) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 with t = A^{1/3} and A = t^3 \in \mathbb{Z}.

Comparison with the color fibration.

The color elliptic curve of Bring's surface is the cubic:

  X^3 + (z + 1)X^2 + (z^2 + z + 1)X
  + (z^3 + z^2 + z + 1) = 0

in the color variable X at spacetime ratio z. The stability cubic and the color cubic are both one-variable cubics parametrized by another variable, arising from the same \chi = -6 surface. The elliptic stability conjecture posits that when the pairing energy lifts the stability cubic to genus 1, the resulting elliptic curve is isogenous to the color fiber.

The n/p ratio.

For each proton number p, the stable neutron number n^*(p) satisfies:

  \frac{n^*(p)}{p}
  = 
  \frac{A^*(p)}{p} - 1
  = 
  1 + c \cdot {A^*}^{2/3}

where A^*(p) solves p = A/(2 + cA^{2/3}). The ratio n/p is a slowly growing function of p. Its integer-part transitions occur at specific elements.

Stable hadrons as integer points on an algebraic curve.

Every stable nucleus corresponds to a lattice point (p, A) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 on the stability cubic \mathcal{S}. The nuclear chart is not a phenomenological fit; it is the set of integer solutions to an algebraic equation determined by the single parameter q.

When the pairing correction lifts \mathcal{S} from genus 0 to genus 1, the stability pairs become rational points of an elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_p over \mathbb{Q}(q). Mordell's theorem constrains them to a finite set. This finite constraint potentially explains why only finitely many stability pairs exist.

Connection to the substrate parameter.

The curvature parameter c = \lambda_C / (2a_{\mathrm{asym}}), with \lambda_C = (q - q^{-1})[6]_q\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{e}}, is controlled entirely by q. At q = 1, the stability cubic degenerates to t^3 = 2p, a rational parametrization where all nuclei are symmetric (n = p). As q increases from 1, the ct^2 term bends the curve. The integer solutions disperse. The structure of the nuclear chart—neutron excess, stability pairs, and even-odd staggering—emerges from a single deformation parameter.
